description: We are Unisonar team, a group of 6 tech-savvy girls who are interested in inclusive and creative solutions, and we have a combination of various skills and interests, such as art creation, making useful applications, sewing, space exploration, global issues, with different background in scientific field (physics, math, computer sciences) and business (statistics, market research etc)
summary:
Earth Information Jukebox is a mobile application built in Kotlin that transforms real-time NASA satellite data into dynamic, 44.1 kHz PCM soundscapes. Directly addressing the challenge, our solution replaces overwhelming visual dashboards with intuitive auditory cues.
Using parallel coroutines, the app ingests live environmental telemetry from NASA POWER (solar radiation, temperature, and aerosols) and NASA EONET v3 (active storms), mapping them onto harmonic chords, sub-bass, and ambient textures. Users can explore global hotspots and adjust individual audio channels in real time.
This project is important because traditional Earth science creates heavy cognitive overload and excludes visually impaired individuals. By translating sight into sound, our app democratizes climate data and serves as an inclusive educational tool.
details: Earth Information Jukebox converts real-time satellite telemetry from NASA POWER and NASA EONET v3 into dynamic, 44.1 kHz PCM soundscapes. Built in Kotlin using Android Studio, Parallel Kotlin Coroutines, and Figma for UI/UX design, the app fetches, cleans, and maps environmental metrics—such as solar radiation, temperature, and storm proximity—into smooth harmonic chords and ambient textures. By replacing complex visual charts with intuitive audio frequencies, it reduces cognitive overload and makes climate data accessible to visually impaired individuals. This multi-sensory approach transforms raw scientific data into an engaging and inclusive educational tool.
